items.maltese: Agħmel lista ta' frott u ħaxix li tħobb tixtri.
items.english: Make a list of fruit and vegetables that you like to buy.

items.maltese: Pereżempju: kilo brunġiel, wiżna patata, żewġ basliet, larinġ, lumi.
items.english: For example: a kilo of aubergines, a sack of potatoes, two onions, oranges, lemons.
We need apples.
I need oranges.

items.maltese: X'inhu l-kollettiv ta' tuffieħa? Il-kollettiv ta' tuffieħa huwa tuffieħ.
items.english: What is the collective of apple? The collective of apple is tuffieħ.

items.maltese: X'inhu l-kollettiv ta' tadama? Il-kollettiv ta' tadama huwa tadam.
items.english: What is the collective of tomato? The collective of tomato is tadam.

items.maltese: Meta nuża l-plural? Nuża l-plural meta rrid ngħid numru speċifiku, bħal żewġ basliet.
items.english: When do I use the plural? I use the plural when I want to say a specific number, such as two onions.

items.maltese: Meta nuża l-kollettiv? Nuża l-kollettiv meta nitkellem fuq ħafna, ftit, kilo jew tip ta' ikel u frott.
items.english: When do I use the collective? I use the collective when I talk about much, a little, a kilo, or a type of food and fruit.

items.maltese: Kif ngħid “fresh fish”? Ngħid ħut frisk.
items.english: How do I say “fresh fish”? I say ħut frisk.

items.maltese: Kif ngħid “good cheese”? Ngħid ġobon tajjeb.
items.english: How do I say “good cheese”? I say ġobon tajjeb.

items.maltese: X'se tixtri mis-suq? Se nixtri ftit ħass, kilo larinġ u naqra brunġiel.
items.english: What will you buy at the market? I will buy some lettuce, a kilo of oranges, and some aubergines.

items.maltese: Għandek bżonn xi frott? Iva, għandi bżonn tuffieħ u lumi.
items.english: Do you need any fruit? Yes, I need apples and lemons.
Green apple, but green apples / apple fruit.
Red tomato, but red tomatoes.
Big onion, but big onions.
Green cucumber, but green cucumbers.
Good loaf of bread, but good bread.
Good cheese, but good cheese in collective use.
Fresh fish, but fish in collective use.
Hardworking bee, but hardworking bees.
Small mosquito, but small mosquitoes.
Dirty fly, but dirty flies.
I need apples.
We need oranges.
I am going to buy a kilo of mandarins.
I would like half a kilo of oranges.

items.maltese: Għandi bżonn kilo u nofs lanġas.
items.english: I need one and a half kilos of pears.
I am going to buy some aubergines.
I want some garlic.
We have a lot of oranges at home.
Today I bought a lot of watermelons.

items.maltese: Għandi żewġ basliet u erba' tadamiet.
items.english: I have two onions and four tomatoes.

items.maltese: Xtrajt żewġ larinġiet u żewġ tewmiet.
items.english: I bought two oranges and two garlic bulbs.

items.maltese: Fil-lista tal-ħaxix ktibt tadam, ħass, brunġiel u ħjar.
items.english: In the vegetable list I wrote tomatoes, lettuce, aubergines, and cucumbers.

items.maltese: Fil-lista tal-frott ktibt tuffieħ, larinġ, mandolin u lanġas.
items.english: In the fruit list I wrote apples, oranges, mandarins, and pears.
I like to buy fresh fruit.
My mother likes to buy fresh vegetables.

items.maltese: Fil-kċina għandna lumi, tuffieħ u bajd.
items.english: In the kitchen we have lemons, apples, and eggs.

items.maltese: Fil-friġġ hemm ġobon tajjeb u ħut frisk.
items.english: In the fridge there is good cheese and fresh fish.
At the market I saw bees and flies.

items.maltese: Ma rridx larinġ għax ma jidhirx frisk.
items.english: I do not want oranges because they do not look fresh.

items.maltese: Illum mort is-suq u xtrajt ftit frott u ħaxix.
items.english: Today I went to the market and bought some fruit and vegetables.
